However, further searching found an active EU-funded CIVIPOL project ('Appui à la Modernisation, à la Sécurisation et à l'Accessibilité du Système d'Etat Civil en RCA'), running since January 2021, which has built a secure digital database in a pilot zone, distributed over 100,000 birth certificates by 2023 and is targeting 400,000 by 2028; a February 2026 project committee review confirms 90% of 2025 activities completed. This is a genuine, ongoing digitisation effort, not yet a nationwide digital civil register, so the score is revised from 1 (No) to 3 (Under development) rather than confirmed as originally stated.
revised_comments: The Central African Republic's civil register remains predominantly paper-based and fragmented across local offices, having lost an estimated 60-80% of records outside Bangui after the 2013 crisis. However, an EU-funded modernisation project implemented by CIVIPOL since 2021 is actively building a secure digital civil registration database in a pilot zone, having issued over 100,000 birth certificates as of 2023 with a target of 400,000 by 2028, placing the digital civil register under active development rather than absent.

revised_comments: The Central African Republic does not maintain an established national social protection register, per the World Bank's 2025 Global Insights on Social Registries. A unified social registry (Registre Social Unique) has been under development with donor support since 2018 but has been repeatedly delayed by limited technical capacity and institutional changes; in the interim, programme-specific beneficiary registries have been built for individual safety-net projects, most recently an interim Beneficiary Operations Management System under the 2024 Ndoyé Project, pending the national registry's completion.
